origin_and_geography.native_tract: Originally from Montgomery district (now Sahiwal), widely conserved and bred across Punjab, Haryana, Northern Rajasthan, and Western Uttar Pradesh, India.
origin_and_geography.agro_climatic_zone: Indo-Gangetic alluvial plains and northern semi-arid sub-tropical zone.
origin_and_geography.historical_background: Regarded as the premier milk-producing zebu breed of the subcontinent. Evolved under pastoral nomadic grazing along the Ravi River. Extensively used worldwide to develop tropical synthetic dairy breeds (e.g. Jamaica Hope, Australian Milking Zebu).

morphological_traits.horns: Short, thick, stubby, growing outward and curving slightly upward.
morphological_traits.forehead: Medium width, flat, masculine in bulls and refined in cows.
morphological_traits.coat_color: Reddish dun, brownish red, or pale red; occasionally with white symmetrical markings.
morphological_traits.ears: Medium size, black-fringed, held horizontally with moderate drop.
morphological_traits.hump_and_dewlap: Massive, fleshy hump in bulls; exceptionally voluminous, loose, pendulous dewlap ('lola') with deep folds.
morphological_traits.body_conformation: Heavy, cylindrical, capacious dairy body; loose skin, well-developed udder with cylindrical teats, long thin tail reaching almost to the ground.

production_and_utility.primary_utility: High-volume dairy production rich in A2 beta-casein.
production_and_utility.draught_capacity: Low to moderate; bullocks are slow and lethargic, used mainly for slow carting.

management_and_resilience.diet_and_forage: High feed conversion efficiency on berseem, maize, mustard cake, and wheat straw.
management_and_resilience.disease_resistance: Outstanding resistance to tick-borne diseases (theileriosis), mastitis, and heat stress.

conservation_status: Priority breed of the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI) and Central Herd Registration Scheme (CHRS).
